Kuvitus: laboratorion pöydällä on kaksi: Illustration: on a laboratory bench there are two glass-domed electroscopes with a shiny zinc plate on top of each. Above the left one a small ultraviolet lamp glows violet, small blue electrons fly from the plate and the leaves of the electroscope hang down. Above the right one a large red lamp shines brightly, but no electrons are released and the leaves of the electroscope are still apart.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: vaakasuora: Schematic figure, not to scale: a horizontal zinc plate at the bottom of the figure. On the left, four photons of red light, wavelength 650 nanometres, hit the plate, drawn as wavy arrows labelled hf. No electrons are released from the plate. On the right, only two photons of ultraviolet light, wavelength 254 nanometres, hit the plate, and from the point of impact of each one a blue electron, e minus, leaves with a velocity arrow, v with a bar above it, pointing up and to the right. A vertical dashed line separates the two situations.
Energiakaavio mittakaavassa natriumille:: Energy diagram to scale for sodium: the lower horizontal line is the energy of the most weakly bound electron in the metal, and the upper one, 2.28 electronvolts higher, is the energy at which an electron just gets free. The difference is the work function W. Three vertical photon arrows start from the lower line, and their length is the photon energy hf. The photon of red light, 650 nanometres and 1.91 electronvolts, stays below the line: hf is smaller than W, and the electron is not released. The photon of green light, 544 nanometres, reaches exactly the line: hf is equal to W. The photon of violet light, 405 nanometres and 3.06 electronvolts, reaches over the line; the part above it, 0.78 electronvolts, is the maximum kinetic energy of the electron, E k max, marked with a blue bracket.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: irtoavien elektro: Graph to scale: the maximum kinetic energy of the released electrons in electronvolts as a function of the frequency of the light, the frequency axis from zero to 16 times 10 to the power 14 hertz. The line for sodium starts on the horizontal axis at the threshold frequency 5.5 times 10 to the power 14 hertz and rises to the value 4.3 electronvolts. The line for zinc starts at the threshold frequency 10.4 times 10 to the power 14 hertz and is parallel to the line for sodium. Below the threshold frequency no electrons are released. On the line for sodium a dashed triangle shows the slope, and the label says that the slope is the Planck constant h.
